title: lm15 gateway capture record, version 1
description: One row of one of the four daily JSONL streams the lm15 gateway writes (exchanges, events, scan, decoded). Ratified 2026-09-19: changes/2026-09-19-capture-record.md. Writers and fixtures validate against the stream's row schema under $defs; readers MUST ignore fields they do not know (C9) — additionalProperties:false here is for writers and fixtures, never a reader's rule. Times are UTC, millisecond precision, RFC 3339 with a Z suffix, so rows sort as strings.

version.description: Capture schema version. Bumped only for a change a v=1 reader would misread (C9).

ulid.description: ULID, Crockford base32, upper case: the first 10 characters encode the millisecond the exchange began, so ids sort by time.

timestamp.description: UTC, millisecond precision, RFC 3339 with Z. Never a local offset.

tag.description: The /t/<tag>/ segment of the base URL, lower-cased by the gateway so 'Pi' and 'pi' are one ledger line. The cost-center / program label.

provider.description: Provider door, hyphen-spelled per spec/vocabularies.md 'Open string namespaces' (openai-codex, bedrock-anthropic). Open: a user-defined upstream is a provider too.

api_family.description: The wire dialect, underscore-spelled per spec/vocabularies.md — the same namespace as api_family on cases. 'unknown' means the gateway could not classify the exchange as a model call it knows (a /v1/models listing, a login refresh, an unrecognised path).

usage.description: spec/types.md Usage, verbatim: provider-reported counters, omit-empty, never re-derived. Which counters include which others differs per provider (the table under Usage); the row's provider says which rule applies.

blob.description: One stored raw message under raw/<sha256[:2]>/<sha256>.http (request or response) or .jsonl (websocket frames). See gateway/README.md 'Raw blobs' for the byte format.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored bytes: the content address. Computed after redaction (C5) and, when a tag opts in, scrubbing (C5b).

wire_sha256.description: The receipt hash over the UNREDACTED transport message, in the format lm15-contract/research/providers/_capture.py already writes: for a request, sha256 of the compact UTF-8 JSON {"method","url","headers":[[name,value],...],"body_b64"} with the unredacted upstream URL, header names in wire case and order, and the body as sent (before any content decoding); for a response, sha256 of the body bytes exactly as received from upstream (before content decoding). Never stored as bytes; this is what AUTHORITY.md requires to promote an exchange into the corpus. Omitted by synthetic examples, required in gateway/captures/.

content_encoding.description: The wire's Content-Encoding (gzip, br, ...) when the stored body is the DECODED entity. The stored headers then omit content-encoding and transfer-encoding and carry a content-length equal to `bytes` minus the header section; this field is the only trace of the original framing.

offset.description: Byte offset into the stored blob.

kind.description: The pattern name, e.g. 'aws access key id' — the names of tools/check_secrecy.py are the seed set.

exchange.title: exchanges/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl — one row per request through the gateway
exchange.description: Written exactly once, when the exchange ends or aborts. The ledger: answers who, which model, how much, how long and how routed with no join. C2.

t.description: First byte received from the application.

t_end.description: Last byte sent to the application. Absent on abort.

origin.description: Who called. user_agent from the request; pid/exe from the loopback peer lookup (best effort, omitted when unknown).

path.description: Path and query as received, after the /t/<tag>/<provider> prefix is stripped and secret query parameters are removed (C5).

url.description: Where the request went after routing. Never carries userinfo; never carries a secret query parameter.

request_id.description: The provider's request id (x-request-id, request-id, x-amzn-requestid, ...), for support tickets and provider dashboards.

ttfb_ms.description: Milliseconds from sending the request upstream to the first response byte.

latency_ms.description: Milliseconds from sending the request upstream to the last response byte.

model.description: Absent when the exchange carries no model (a listing, a login call). When present, asked and sent are both written even when equal: the ledger must not need a join to answer 'was it rerouted?'.

served.description: What the response named (often a dated snapshot).

route.description: Absent means no rule matched: pass-through.

adaptations.description: MAP-13 records from a translate lane; the same type as Response.adaptations. Omitted when empty.

error.description: Present when the gateway failed or refused, or as the canonical summary of a provider error (whose bytes are in the raw response).

feature.description: CapabilityError.feature: the config path a refusal is about.

redacted.description: Lower-cased header names, and 'query:<name>' for query parameters, whose values were removed before storage (C5). Always present, possibly empty: an auditor sees what was removed without seeing it.

secrets.description: C5b. Present only when the body scan matched.

locations.description: Where, when marked (the default). Omitted when scrubbed: the bytes are gone.

response.description: For sse, the complete stream text. Absent on abort before any response byte.

frames.description: websocket only: the frame log (README 'Raw blobs').

event.title: events/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl — one row per wire frame
event.description: When each piece of a reply arrived and how big it was. Content is not repeated here: the raw response (or frames) blob holds it verbatim. A non-streamed reply is one row (seq 0). C3.

dir.description: websocket only: in = from upstream to the application, out = from the application to upstream.

event.description: The SSE event name (Anthropic, Responses) or the JSON 'type' of a frame when the wire names frames that way; absent on wires that do not (Chat Completions chunks). Lets timing analysis (first content vs ping) run without opening blobs.

scan.title: scan/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl — one row per observed program→provider connection
scan.description: The coverage view's input (boundary D8, C4). No root, no certificate: connection tables and process names only.

host.description: Provider hostname when known (api.openai.com); absent when only the address matched a range.

match.description: ip: the address matched a provider host the gateway resolved itself. dns: the optional privileged helper saw the lookup of `host` precede the connection (definitive).

shared_range.description: True when the matched address is on a CDN range shared with unrelated services (Cloudflare fronts api.openai.com and chatgpt.com): the match is probable, not certain. Omitted when false.

coverage.description: covered: the connection is to the gateway itself. observed: reached a provider directly; a recipe may exist. observed_not_coverable: no known way to route this program.

recipe.description: Knowledge-base entry that would cover this program (cursor, zed, aider, ...).

decoded.title: decoded/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl — one row per decoder pass over one exchange
decoded.description: Joined to exchanges on id. Written later, possibly by another program and another SDK; two decoders may each write a row for one id and readers pick by decoder or contract_pin, never 'last wins'. An exchange with no decoded row is pending. C2b.

contract_pin.description: The lm15-contract commit the decoder implements; the canonical types below are that pin's.

status.description: full: request and response both decoded. partial: something was not (notes says what and why; the raw bytes are still there). none: api_family unknown, or a call on a provider host that is not a model call.

request.description: Canonical Request (spec/types.md) as the decoder read it from the raw request. Validated by the SDK's own deserializer against its pin, not by this schema: the canonical types are specified by spec/types.md and serde/canonical.json, which have no JSON Schema rendering yet.

response.description: Canonical Response, including adaptations and provider_data as the SDK produces them.

events.description: The canonical post-coalesce event trace (MAP-3/4) for a streamed exchange, in the order of the events stream rows.
